newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money higher on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money higher on tight liquidity.

text.p: Jakarta call money remained expensive as the central bank maintained a tight money policy.
Overnight money eased to 20.0/21.0 percent from an early high of 28.0 percent. But the market remained wary.
One local bank dealer said rupiah demand was still high, probably due to last Friday's purchase of dollars and also due to weekly tax payments due Tuesday.
She said people were concerned over a tighter condition on Wednesday if the central bank did not allow roll-overs of some 200 billion rupiah maturing repo papers from last week.
Longer-term rates were on the rise following an extended tight policy in the short-end market. One- and three-month money were both at 18.5/19.0 percent.
But one-week money was at 20.0/21.0 percent.

Another dealer said inverse interest rates in the money market resulted from operators' expectation that the tight money policy currently imposed by the central bank was temporary and could change once the foreign exchange market stabilised.
The bank kept its interest rates for short-term bilateral papers (SBIs) unchanged on Tuesday and did not offer repos and remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.

The bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-six day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 21.49 percent, compared with 19.62 percent last Friday.
